Abstract.AbstractText: The median arcuate ligament (MAL) is a fibrous arch connecting the right and left diaphragmatic crura; this usually lies superior to the origin of the coeliac axis. Occasionally, the ligament crosses anterior to the aorta, at the level of the coeliac trunk; leading to mechanical compression of the coeliac artery, resulting in the clinical condition of MAL syndrome (MALS). Symptomatic patients characteristically present with post-prandial pain associated with unintentional weight loss, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. An open or laparoscopic surgical approach is used to divide the median arcuate ligament allowing decompression of the coeliac artery. The authors report two unique cases of MALS with exertion-induced abdominal pain in young competitive athletes for the second time in the literature since 200419. Both cases highlight how the rarity of MALS combined with a lack of typical symptomatology such as post-prandial abdominal pain can challenge diagnosis. Despite the scarcity of available guidelines for management of MALS, with several clinicians relying on subset analyses of surgical outcomes, the excellent clinical response to surgery in both of our patients suggest that treatment can be delivered by less invasive surgical techniques with successful outcomes.
